name: Smoky black bean & pepper burgers
subtitle: A burgers supper using ready-cooked vegetables and pulses.

swap.reason: Use unsweetened plant-based yogurt for the finishing sauce. The recipe specifies dairy-free bread, pastry or cheese wherever those are used; check package labels.

steps: Prepare the filling

Drain canned black beans, drained well and rinse if canned. Finely chop cooked roasted bell pepper and drain excess moisture. Both the pulses and vegetables must already be cooked. Measure smoked paprika; reserve lemon juice and yogurt for the finish.
Shape the patties

Mash canned black beans, drained thoroughly. Mix with finely chopped cooked roasted bell pepper, smoked paprika, oats and chickpea flour. Rest 10 minutes so oats absorb moisture. Form four thin patties; if crumbly add water a teaspoon at a time, or if too wet add a little more oats.
Cook
Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook patties 5–6 minutes per side until firm, browned and hot throughout. Turn gently; cook in batches if necessary.
Assemble
Warm the buns. Add lettuce and two small patties per bun. Serve extra patties alongside if your buns are small.
Finish and serve
Stir lemon juice into {finish}. Season the dish to taste and serve with the lemon yogurt alongside or spooned over.

swap.reason: Use unsweetened plant-based yogurt for the finishing sauce. The recipe specifies dairy-free bread, pastry or cheese wherever those are used; check package labels.

steps: Prepare the filling

Drain canned black beans, drained well and rinse if canned. Finely chop cooked roasted bell pepper and drain excess moisture. Both the pulses and vegetables must already be cooked. Measure smoked paprika; reserve lemon juice and yogurt for the finish.
Make the filling
Mash half of canned black beans, drained and combine with cooked roasted bell pepper and smoked paprika. Spread thinly over half of each tortilla, add plant-based cheese, then fold closed.
Toast

Brush a wide nonstick skillet with olive oil over medium-low heat. Cook folded tortillas 3–4 minutes per side, in batches, until crisp and the filling is hot. Follow cheese melting instructions; lower heat if tortillas brown too quickly.
Slice
Rest for a minute, then cut into wedges. Keep completed quesadillas warm while cooking the rest.

Stir lemon juice into {finish}. Season the dish to taste and serve with the lemon yogurt alongside or spooned over.

swap.reason: Use unsweetened plant-based yogurt for the finishing sauce. The recipe specifies dairy-free bread, pastry or cheese wherever those are used; check package labels.

steps: Prepare the filling

Drain cooked green lentils well and rinse if canned. Finely chop cooked beetroot and drain excess moisture. Both the pulses and vegetables must already be cooked. Measure dried dill; reserve lemon juice and yogurt for the finish.
Cook the gnocchi
Cook gnocchi in simmering water following its packet instructions, then drain. Reserve a small cup of the cooking water.
Make the sauce

Heat olive oil over medium heat. Add cooked green lentils, cooked beetroot and dried dill and tomato passata. Simmer for 8 minutes until the filling is hot throughout. Loosen with a splash of gnocchi water.
Combine
Fold cooked gnocchi into the sauce and heat together for 1–2 minutes without crushing them.
Finish and serve
Stir lemon juice into {finish}. Season the dish to taste and serve with the lemon yogurt alongside or spooned over.

swap.reason: Use unsweetened plant-based yogurt for the finishing sauce. The recipe specifies dairy-free bread, pastry or cheese wherever those are used; check package labels.

steps: Prepare the filling

Drain canned white beans, drained well and rinse if canned. Finely chop cooked mushrooms and drain excess moisture. Both the pulses and vegetables must already be cooked. Measure dried thyme; reserve lemon juice and yogurt for the finish.
Start the base
Dice onion. Heat olive oil in a deep pan and soften onion for 5 minutes. Stir in tomato paste and dry orzo.
Simmer

Add broth and canned white beans, drained, cooked mushrooms and dried thyme. Simmer gently for the orzo package cooking time, usually 10–12 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking. Add hot water if it becomes dry before the orzo is tender.
Check and rest
Check that orzo is tender and the whole dish is hot throughout. Rest off the heat for 2 minutes before serving.
Finish and serve
Stir lemon juice into {finish}. Season the dish to taste and serve with the lemon yogurt alongside or spooned over.
